chunks: And from him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who performed ghusl (ritual bath) from janābah, or on the day of Jumuʿah, or on the day of ʿĪd: is wudu (ablution) required of him before that or after it? He said: No, neither before nor after; the ghusl suffices for him. And the woman is likewise in that: if she performs ghusl from hayd or other than that, then wudu (ablution) is not required of her, neither before nor after; the ghusl suffices for her.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهَا: it sufficed her; it fulfilled the required purification
key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it sufficed him; it fulfilled the required purification
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ghusl (ritual bath), a full-body purification that suffices in the cases mentioned
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the minor ritual purification otherwise required for salat (prayer)
key_terms.جَنَابَةٍ: state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.حَيْضٍ: menstruation, after which ghusl is performed
key_terms.يَوْمَ جُمُعَةٍ: the day of Friday, referring here to the ghusl of Jumuʿah
key_terms.يَوْمَ عِيدٍ: the day of ʿĪd, referring here to the ghusl of ʿĪd

ai.seo_question: Does ghusl remove the need for wudu (ablution) before or after it in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that ghusl is sufficient and removes the need for wudu (ablution), both before and after it, in the cases mentioned. The ruling applies to both men and women, including ghusl for janābah, Jumuʿah, ʿĪd, and hayd.
